newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Index vols firm in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Index vols firm in slow trade.

text.p: Implied volatilites for U.S. stock index options rebounded a little from Friday's depressed levels, although trading was subdued by the absence of many traders for Columbus Day, traders said.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) Volatility Index was up 0.28 point to 15.79 at 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, even as the S&P 100 index .OEX gained 5.15 points to 682.45.
Traders expected choppy trading this week due to the expiration of October options at the end of the week, with expiration-linked trades probably benefitting the market in the coming few days.
"The boat is loaded with put buying that's occurred for three weeks to this point," said Jerry Hegarty, chief equity analyst at Thomson Research.

He said a large number of people long puts should support the market for a few more sessions, sending December S&P 500 index futures SPZ6 and the OEX to fresh highs. December S&P futures were up 3.50 points to 709.40, very close to their all-time high of 710.60.
Still, Chris Bookmyer, a designated primary market-maker at CBOE, said she was cautious about the possibility of some negative surprises.
"I'm looking this week for a earnings-driven market," Bookmyer said, noting that firms like Intel Corp, Microsoft Corp and Compaq Computer Corp were due to release their earnings this week.
"Intel is expected to be strong, and the tech sector has been strong, but I still have a little caution because I still expect a mixed bag (of earnings results)," she said.

Intel's stock was up 1-1/4 to 106-5/8 in late morning trade. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index .SOXX was up 3.66 points to 199.36, after briefly popping above the 200 mark earlier in the day on modest options volume.
Bookmyer added that Wednesday's September U.S. consumer price data were also keeping the market somewhat tense, even though Friday's producer prices were benign.
"Going into expiration week, Mondays are like this -- a mishmash of indicators," said Tim Ord of analytical publication Ord Oracle.
Ord said he was bullish in the longer term towards the end of the year, but that he expected a corrective move down sometime in the near term, perhaps after the October expirations.
The McClellan oscillator had marked three peaks recently, with the last two lower than the first one, while stock prices ground higher, he noted.
"Normally when you get a divergence like that, it's a warning that a top is not far off," he said.

High uptick readings in the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) tick indicator on the previous two Fridays would also be confirmed as a bearish signal if they are joined by a bearish candlestick pattern today, he added.
